column2: for a Vaishya in the twelfth from conception — not later than sixteen years. The girdles are declared in order of munja grass, bark-cord (for the other two);
deer, tiger-skins are for those who observe the vow; the staffs in order are of palasha, pipal and bilva;
they are said in order to be equal to the hair, forehead and face; all straight, with bark, unscorched are the staffs.
The garment and the sacred thread are of cotton, linen and wool in order; the word "bhavat" is marked at the beginning, middle and end.
He should first beg where alms are certain. For women these are without mantra; the marriage is with mantra.
Having initiated, the teacher should teach the pupil first purity, conduct, the fire-rite and twilight worship.
Facing east one eats long life; facing south one eats fame; facing west one eats prosperity; facing north one eats truth.
Morning and evening one should offer; one should avoid the impure, the open hand, honey, meat, song and dance with people;
violence, slander of others, and especially obscenity. One should carry a staff and the like; if lost, one should throw it in water and take another.
Having completed the taking up of the Veda one should bathe, having given the teacher's fee.
In five calamities a different husband is prescribed for women: when the husband is dead, to the brother-in-law should she be given; in his absence as she wishes.
The three Purvas, Agni's, Vayavya and the three Uttaras, and Rohini — in the foot, the star-group is always praised.
One should not choose one of the same gotra nor of the same sage-line, Bhargava; beyond the seventh on the father's side and the fifth on the mother's.
The gift after invitation to one endowed with family and character is the Brahma marriage; the son born of it saves his men always through the gift of a maiden.
Likewise from the taking of a pair of cattle the marriage is called Arsha; given to one who asks is Prajapatya, he who does dharma.
By price the Asura, base; by mutual choice the Gandharva; by capture in battle the Rakshasa; by deceit of a girl the Paishacha.
On the wedding day one should make a pure one from a potter's clay; having worshipped her at a water-place with instruments and the rest, the wife should guard the home.
When Keshava is asleep marriage is not to be done at all; in Pausha and Chaitra, on Tuesday, in empty or Vishti days, not.
Not when Venus or Jupiter are set; not when the moon is afflicted by planets; not in a star joined with Sun, Saturn and Mars, nor struck by Vyatipata.
Mrigashira, the ancestral star, Vayavya, Savitra, Rohini, the three Uttaras, Mula, Mitra and Pushan are the marriage stars.
The ascendant called human and the human navamsha are auspicious; in the third, sixth, tenth, eleventh and eighth,
Sun, Saturn, Moon and Mercury are praised, not Mars in the eighth; in the seventh, last and eighth groups the rest are praised as best planets;
of them too Venus in the sixth from the middle is not praised. At the marriage star the fourth ceremony should likewise be done;
the planets there are not to be given, the fourth and the others alone. One should approach his wife except on parva days; with truthful gift, union is always.
One should not converse with a menstruating woman and outcastes; one should remember Keshava. One should not laugh, yawn or sneeze with mouth uncovered;
the wise should conceal even disrespect of a lord; he should not oppose the senses nor cause obstruction to the Veda.
No disease should be neglected, nor even a small enemy, Bhargava. One who crosses the road should always rinse; one should not carry fire and water together.
One should not say "hum" to Shiva, who is worthy of worship; one should not tread on a foot with a foot; one should not say anything unpleasant to anyone, present or absent;
one should avoid blaming Veda, scripture, kings, sages and gods; one should not be jealous of women; one should avoid trusting them;
one should daily hear dharma and love the gods and practice dharma and the rest; on the birth star worship of the Moon, worship of Brahmins, gods and the rest;
one should avoid oil-anointing on the sixth, fourteenth and eighth; from afar from the house of urine and feces; one should not do enmity with superiors.
Of water-born things and vessels and everything made of stone, of vegetables, ropes, roots, fruits and bamboo,
of sacrificial vessels by wiping with the hand in sacrificial rites; of those with grease by hot water; the house by sweeping:
cloth by cleaning and beating; purification by clay and water; for much cloth by sprinkling; of wooden things by planing;
of those joined together by sprinkling and of liquids by decanting; of beds, seats, vehicles, a winnowing basket and a cart,
purification is to be known by sprinkling; of straw and fuel likewise; of pure objects by paste; of horn and ivory things
by cow-hair; of flesh-vessels and bones as of horn; of resins, jaggery and salts by drying;
of safflower flowers and of wool and cotton; pure is water that has gone into a river; so too water spread out.
The cow is pure except the mouth; pure is the mouth of the horse and goat; of women, calves and birds and the dog's mouth,
in the flow of the mouths in hunting is always pure. Having eaten, sneezed, slept, drunk, bathed,
having crossed a road one should rinse and change clothes; the cat is pure by walking; the menstruating woman on the fourth day;
the bathed woman on the fifth is fit for divine and ancestral rites. Five for the anus, ten for one hand, seven for both hands in clays;
one clay for the organ, three or two for the hands; for students, forest-dwellers and ascetics four times as much.
With shri-fruits for silk garments, with white mustard for linen, purification is declared by sprinkling with water for deer-hair;
of flowers and fruits the whole by sprinkling with water.
By three nights her kin are purified, no doubt here. One who has obtained purification equal should end it by the first;
unequal by the second, as the king of Dharma's word. One living in another country on hearing of births and deaths in his family
is impure for the remaining part of the ten nights. When the ten nights are passed he is impure for three nights;
when a year has passed he is purified by bathing alone; and when a maternal grandfather or a teacher has died;
in miscarriage purification by nights equal to the months. For a Brahmin among sapindas all castes without distinction
are purified in ten nights; a king in twelve days; Vaishyas in fifteen days; Shudras in a month, Bhargava.
Near the leavings one should offer one pinda and proclaim his name and gotra, composed.
When the best Brahmins have eaten and been honored with wealth, with rice and water released and the gotra and name announced,
a pit four fingers wide, that much apart, a span long should be made; likewise three for the Vikarshus.
Near the Vikarshus one should kindle three fires: for Soma, Agni and Yama, Rama, in brief;
one should properly offer oblations, everywhere four and three. One should place pindas as before, separately.
One should fill with rice, curds, honey and meat. If there is an intercalary month in the middle, one should do more.
Or one should complete all this in twelve days. If there is an intercalary month in the middle of the year,
then in the twelve-month rite more should be done. When the year is complete one should perform the ancestral rite like an ancestral rite.
For the departed, then afterward, in the three generations of him, one should place pindas, and likewise four, composed.
Having worshipped and given, with "Earth is equal," one should join the ghost's pinda with the other pindas, Bhargava.
The ghost's vessel too should be placed among the vessels. This rite is to be done separately for each in the ritual vessel.
This rite without mantra is prescribed for a Shudra. For women the Sapindikarana should be done thus.
One should perform the ancestral rite every year for the departed, a pot of food for a year. As the sands of the Ganga, as rain in Indra's season,
can be counted in the world but not the past grandfathers; in ever-moving time there is no steadiness; therefore one should act.
In the state of godhood or in a place of torment the ghost obtains the rite performed; a man grieving should not benefit the ghost or himself.
For those dead by falling from a cliff, fire, noose, poison or water, suicides and outcastes, there is no impurity, and those slain by lightning or weapon;
ascetics, vow-keepers, students, kings, craftsmen, the initiated and those who do the king's bidding — he should bathe even when following a corpse.
After intercourse and in the smoke of a funeral pile immediate bathing is prescribed. A Brahmin should not carry a corpse by a Shudra in any way;
nor a Shudra by a Brahmin; fault arises for both. By carrying the corpse of a helpless Brahmin one shares the heavenly world;
he gains victory in battle; and one who gives wood for a helpless corpse. Having designated the kinsman ghost, with the left-turned circuit of the pyre,
all should bathe with their clothes; they should give the ghost three handfuls of water each,
having placed the foot on a stone at the door they should enter the house; one should throw rice in the fire, having bitten a neem leaf;
they should sleep separately on the ground, and eat bought or obtained food. One pinda on the tenth day; the shaven one is pure.
The wise should bathe with mustard and sesame, wearing another cloth. For a child without teeth, an infant, or in miscarriage
there is no cremation nor water-rite; on the fourth day and the gathering of bones should be done.
After the gathering of bones, touching the limbs is prescribed.
For those who die from calamity, in cremating knowers of Brahman, in a sacrifice-session, vowed students, in battle, in disturbance of the country,
in giving, sacrifice and marriage, immediate purity is prescribed. For killers of Brahmins, cows and kings and suicides, it is unstated;
for one with an incurable disease and incapable of study, expiation is permitted: entering fire or water.
From insult, anger, affection, contempt or fear, a woman or man dies hanged in any way;
the suicide dwells a hundred thousand years in a hot hell. An old man, lapsed from Vedic and Smarta practice, who gives up his breath —
three nights impurity there; on the second the gathering of bones; on the third the water-rite; on the fourth the ancestral rite.
For those slain by lightning or fire, three days' purification for the sapinda. Women who rely on heresies or kill their husbands have no impurity or water-rite.
At the death of father, mother and others, wet-clothed, fasting; when a year has passed one should perform the ghost-rite by rule.
Whoever carries a non-sapinda corpse in any way is purified by bathing with clothes on, touching fire and tasting ghee.
If one eats their food he is purified in ten days; not eating food for a day he should not dwell in that house.
Twice-born who carry a helpless Brahmin corpse gain the fruit of a sacrifice at every step; purification by bathing alone.
A twice-born following a Shudra corpse is pure after three days. Having mourned with the dead one's kin,
one should avoid that day and night gifts, ancestral rites and so on at will. In the house of a Shudra woman's childbirth and a Shudra's death likewise.
